en: The state of being captive.
The state or period of being imprisoned, confined, or enslaved.

captivity.ety: From Middle English captivite, from Latin captīvitās. By surface analysis, captive + -ity. Entered into the English lexicon around the 14th century.

ex.ja: 彼は捕虜になった。

note.ja: cap（つかむ）+ tiv + ity。つかまえられていること →「監禁・捕らわれの身」。captive（捕虜）。

en: Acting as a complement; making up a whole with something else.
Of the specific pairings of the bases in DNA and RNA.
A complementary colour.
An angle which adds with another to equal ninety degrees.

complementary.ety: From complement + -ary. Piecewise doublet of complimentary.

ex.ja: テレビと新聞は互いの機能を補完しあっている。

en: An injury to part of the body, most especially the brain, caused by a violent blow, followed by loss of function.

concussion.ety: From Latin concussiō. Equivalent to concuss + -ion.

ex.ja: 脳震盪だとお医者さんに言われました。

ex.en: I had a concussion.
ex.ja: 脳しんとうを起こしました。

The office of a consul, in its various senses.

consulate.ety: From Middle English consulat, consulate, from Latin consulātus, from consul + -ātus. In some senses, via French consulat. By surface analysis, consul + -ate (forms nouns denoting rank or office).

ex.ja: 彼はアメリカ領事館に出かけたよ。

ex.en: I work at the consulate.
ex.ja: 領事館で働いています。

ex.ja: 私はこのビザを、神戸のアメリカ領事館でとりました。

en: To be in opposition; to contest; to dispute; to vie; to quarrel; to fight.
To struggle or exert oneself to obtain or retain possession of, or to defend.

contend.ety: From Middle English contenden, borrowed from Old French contendre, from Latin contendere (“to stretch out, extend, strive after, contend”), from com- (“together”) + tendere (“to stretch”); see tend, and compare attend, extend, intend, subtend.

ex.en: They contended with each other for the prize.
ex.ja: 彼らは賞を取ろうとお互いに競った。

ex.en: He had to contend against physical suffering.
ex.ja: 彼は肉体の苦痛と闘わねばならなかった。

ex.en: Several teams are contending for the prize.
ex.ja: いくつかのチームがその賞を勝ち取ろうと競い合っています。

note.ja: con（共に）+ tend（伸ばす・張る）。互いに張り合う →「争う・強く主張する」。

en: A strong desire; yearning.

craving.ety: From Middle English cravinge, from Old English crafing (“claim, demand”); equivalent to crave + -ing.

ex.en: I have a craving for fresh fruit.
ex.ja: 新鮮な果物が食べたいんだ。

ex.en: I've been craving frozen yogurt.
ex.ja: フローズン・ヨーグルトが食べたくてしょうがないんだよ。

ex.en: I suddenly got a craving to eat some crisp roast chicken skin.
ex.ja: 急激にかりかりした鳥皮が食べたくなった。

en: Relating to the practice of cookery or the activity of cooking.
Of or relating to a kitchen.

culinary.ety: Borrowed from French culinaire, itself a borrowing from Latin culīnārius, from culīna (“kitchen”).

en: A loud noise; a cacophony or loud commotion.
To make a din, to resound.
(of a place) To be filled with sound, to resound.

din.ety:
From Middle English dyne, dynne, from Old English dyne, from Proto-West Germanic *duni, from Proto-Germanic *duniz, from Proto-Indo-European *dʰún-is, from *dʰwen- (“to make a noise”).
Cognate with English tone, Sanskrit धुनि (dhúni, “sounding”), ध्वनति (dhvánati, “to make a noise, to roar”), Old Norse dynr, Norwegian Nynorsk dynja, Swedish dån, dön.

ex.en: His voice was heard above the din.
ex.ja: 彼の声が騒音にも負けずに聞こえた。

en: Separate; distinct; individual; non-continuous.
That can be perceived individually, not as connected to, or part of, something else.

discrete.ety: From Old French discret, from Latin discrētus, past participle of discernō (“divide”), from dis- + cernō (“sift”). Doublet of discreet.

note.ja: dis（離れて）+ cret（ふるい分ける）+ e。ふるい分けられた →「別々の・個別の」。discreet（慎重な）と同語源で綴りが違う。

en: To disagree; to withhold assent. Construed with from (or, formerly, to).
To differ from, especially in opinion, beliefs, etc.
Disagreement with the ideas, doctrines, decrees, etc. of a political party, government or religion.
An act of disagreeing with, or deviating from, the views and opinions of those holding authority.

dissent.ety: From Middle English dissenten, from Latin dissentiō, dissentīre (“to differ in sentiments, disagree, be at odds, contradict, quarrel”), from dis- + sentiō, sentīre (see sense).

ex.en: He dissented from the opinion of the majority.
ex.ja: 彼は大多数の意見に異議を唱えた。

ex.en: I dissent from what he said.
ex.ja: 私は彼の言ったことに反対する。

ex.en: Within the rape crisis movement, Greensite's dissent is significant.
ex.ja: レイプ危機運動の内部においては、グリーンサイトによる異議表明は重要な意義を持っている。

note.ja: dis（離れて）+ sent（感じる）。違うように感じる →「異議（を唱える）」。consent（同意）と対。

en: Noteworthy, remarkable, great.
Distinguished, important, noteworthy.

eminent.ety: From Middle French éminent, from Latin present participle ēminēns, ēminentis, from verb ēmineō (“to project, protrude”), from ex- (“out of, from”) + mineō, related to mons (English mount). Compare with imminent. Unrelated to emanate, which is instead from mānō (“to flow”). Displaced native Old English deal.

ex.en: He is eminent both as a teacher and writer.
ex.ja: 彼は教師としても作家としても著名である。

ex.en: He is eminent for his great discoveries.
ex.ja: 彼はいくつもの大発見で有名だ。

ex.en: Mr Smith is an eminent violinist.
ex.ja: スミス氏は著名なバイオリニストである。
